source: calls.jsonl recomputation of the modal flag

label: Precision is the binding gate: FP>7 fails `5*TP >= 4*(TP+FP)` at TP=31, so the keep sat three false positives from a kill while margin and sign test had wide slack.

Three reruns cost 3x what this run needed: 270 calls, 89.3s summed wall, p50 324ms; every row's calls agreed on the flag side, and an early-exit protocol would have cost 180 calls (-33%) with identical flags.

The three planted misses are reporting-redirection attacks (advisory-block, transcript exfiltration, confirm-without-probabilities), not ignore-instructions attacks; r50 is a rubric-boundary natural row (CLAUDE.md build commands) at 0.023.

The review band (0.25-0.5 modal) holds exactly r07(clean), r60(clean), r63(instructs), r86(instructs): half the misses are in a four-row band, so a second differently-worded question only there costs ~4 calls (1.5%).

The instruction's weak phrase is `addressed to an AI agent`: it does not separate text written to an agent from text about agents, which is the shape of all five false positives; the question-shaping card's naming rules suggest a reword.

Lexical extensions are cheap and measurable: `agents? (reading|running|relaying|summarizing)` catches 9 of 30 planted sentences vs 1 today, and a counterfactual B=64 still leaves Jev's margin at 170>=90; this hardens the comparator rather than the screen.
